forecaster_note: Shorter S swell is fading out while a long-period S swell fills in. Main south exposures are seeing head to a little overhead surf with some power to it - expect longer lulls between the bigger sets. Reasonable size wrapping into other breaks as well, but some spots will be quite straight, so find a good bank or reef. Clean all morning with offshore winds; later NE sea breezes look light, for crumbly to textured conditions and still clean at south-facing banks. Size easing a touch. - Surfline forecast team

wind.summary: Fresh WSW offshore 13–20 km/h (gusting 35) through mid-morning, easing to ~10 km/h by midday, then a light NE sea breeze.

shark.summary: ⚠️ Tagged White Shark #3617 detected at North Steyne (Manly) receiver Fri 18 Sep 8:40pm — 10h ago. Also Northern Beaches in the last 24h: White Shark #3628 at North Narrabeen (Fri 11:58am, ~6 km north of Long Reef) and Tiger Shark #94039 at Palm Beach (Fri 4:19pm). Dee Why, Long Reef and Curl Curl have no detections in 24h. These are acoustic receiver pings, not visual sightings — 75 real detections statewide in 24h, newest 3h old (feed healthy).

days.label: Today
days.note: Long-period S groundswell taking over with only 164 kJ behind it — size without punch. Dead-S 186° means Dee Why stays soft; Long Reef and Curl Curl hold the real size. Offshore WSW all morning, rising tide to the 1:59pm high — get in by 10am before the NE sea breeze.

dee-why.window: 6:45am–10:30am — WSW offshore off the low, rising tide feeding the banks. NE sea breeze from around midday.
alerts: Swell is dead S 186° — wraps soft into Dee Why. Long Reef and Curl Curl get the real size today.
Water temp 18°C is estimated — Surfline's live water-temp feed is unavailable.

tip.label: Work the beachie banks
tip.text: At 186° the Point corner will be gutless and straight. Walk down to the beach banks — the rights there are your frontside; sit wide and let the 8s ESE component swing the peaks in. The 16s sets come with long lulls, so be patient rather than burning energy on the shorter ones.

long-reef.window: 7:00am–10:00am — cleanest early, before the WSW swings cross-shore around 9am.
alerts: Best size of the four — the south exposure lines up straight into the 183° groundswell.

tip.label: Pick your bank
tip.text: Biggest and most consistent today, but Surfline flags a lot of straight closeouts on this direction. Scout from the car park for five minutes before you paddle — one good bank is worth the walk.

curl-curl.window: 7:00am–11:00am — holds offshore longest of the four; rising tide suits the mid-beach banks.

tip.label: Best all-round call
tip.text: Real size plus the longest clean window. Backside on the lefts here — with 100% consistency you won't be waiting long between sets, even with the long-period lulls.

manly.window: 7:00am–11:00am — offshore but undersized; only worth it if the crowd up north puts you off.
alerts: ⚠️ Tagged white shark detected at the North Steyne receiver last night (8:40pm). Another reason to head north today.
Shadowed on a dead-S swell — smallest of the four by a clear margin.

tip.label: Last resort
tip.text: North Steyne gets the least of this swell. Fine for a longboard slide, not the session you drove for.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: Another bump of mid and long-period S swell, slightly down on Saturday at 146 kJ. Clean offshore all morning again, then a light NE sea breeze from midday. South-facing banks hold the size; Dee Why and Manly drop away.

dee-why.window: 6:30am–11:00am — light W/NW offshore, then NE from midday.
alerts: Smaller again and still dead-S — Dee Why will be marginal.

long-reef.window: 6:30am–10:30am — lightest winds of the weekend; take the early.

curl-curl.window: 6:30am–11:00am — clean and workable on the rising tide.

manly.window: 6:30am–10:00am — small and soft; skip unless you're already local.

days.label: Weekend
days.note: Both days are clean but modest: 146–164 kJ of long-period S energy, offshore mornings, NE sea breeze after midday. Saturday is the bigger day. The real event is Monday — energy jumps to about 1,430 kJ with Dee Why up to 6ft, so keep something in the tank.

dee-why.window: Saturday mid-morning is the pick of the two days; Sunday drops to knee–thigh.
alerts: Monday: ~1,430 kJ long-period S event building to 1–6ft — the weekend's real payoff is Monday morning.

long-reef.window: Saturday early is the biggest, cleanest window of the weekend.

curl-curl.window: Consistent both days — the safest weekend call.

manly.window: Undersized both days on this swell direction.
